title: Psychometry - Its Science and Law of Unfoldment
author: J. C. F. Grumbine
description: Psychometry: Its Science and Law of Unfoldment (second edition) by J. C. F. Grumbine, President of the College of Psychical Sciences and Unfoldment and a prominent American Spiritualist teacher of the early twentieth century. Psychometry, a term coined by Joseph Rodes Buchanan in 1842, is the claimed faculty of reading the history, character or emotional imprint of a person, place or object through touch. Grumbine presents it as a natural spiritual sense that can be systematically developed, explaining its theory in terms of soul, aura and the 'soul of things', distinguishing it from clairvoyance and mediumship, and setting out the laws, conditions and exercises for unfolding it. Part of his series of textbooks on psychic development, it documents how Spiritualist circles framed psychic abilities as a teachable science.
